# Intro Styles Reference

Three distinct creator styles, each targeting a different emotional entry point.

---

## Style 1: Belief Attack (Hormozi)

**Emotional target:** Frustration / Shame / Cognitive dissonance  
**Mechanism:** Opens by attacking a widely held belief or behavior. Makes the viewer feel called out (guilty) OR validated (finally, someone said it).

**Example:**
> *"Poor people stay poor because they want a fast way to get rich. And instead, the richest people that I know pick one of these four paths, play it for a decade, and then end up with more money than everyone else that is just chasing shortcuts."*

**When to use:**
- The viewer is making an obvious mistake they don't realize
- You want a blunt, no-nonsense tone
- The topic involves common misconceptions or self-sabotage

**Line 1 Formula:**
> `"[Group] [stay stuck / stay broke / stay overwhelmed] because they [common wrong behavior]."`

**Tone:** Confrontational, direct, high-energy. Every word earns its place.

---

## Style 2: Injustice Hook (Priestley)

**Emotional target:** Injustice / Envy / Unfairness  
**Mechanism:** Indicts a system or industry, making the viewer feel like a victim of external forces — then positions the creator as the guide who can help them beat the rigged game.

**Example:**
> *"The way income in your industry is distributed is not fair. The people at the top earn way more than everybody else combined. Technology is moving all the money to the top of the power law."*

**When to use:**
- The topic involves an industry, platform, or system with winners and losers
- The viewer feels like they're doing everything right but not getting results
- You want to introduce a systemic/structural insight

**Line 1 Formula:**
> `"The way [system/industry/game] works is not [fair / honest / what you think]."`

**Tone:** Analytical, calm authority. Builds dread before the solution.

---

## Style 3: Empathy Mirror (Srivatsaa)

**Emotional target:** Overwhelm / Exhaustion / Quiet desperation  
**Mechanism:** Opens with "you" — literally begins in the viewer's experience. No judgment. Meets them exactly where they are, validates the feeling, then delivers the reframe.

**Example:**
> *"You can follow all the right money rules and still feel like you're never getting ahead. You can save more and invest early and work hard and still that scoreboard never moves."*

**When to use:**
- The topic involves personal effort that hasn't paid off
- Viewer is trying hard but feeling stuck
- You want a warm, storytelling tone

**Line 1 Formula:**
> `"You can [do the right thing] and [do the right thing] and still [not get the result]."`

**Tone:** Warm, empathetic, storytelling. Every viewer should feel *seen*.

---

## Choosing Your Style

| If the viewer is... | Use |
|--------------------|-----|
| Making an obvious mistake | Belief Attack |
| Doing everything right and still losing | Empathy Mirror |
| Stuck in a system that's rigged against them | Injustice Hook |
| Confused about why effort isn't working | Empathy Mirror |
| Chasing the wrong thing | Belief Attack |
| Unaware of a structural shift in their industry | Injustice Hook |

---

## Tone-Matching Rule

Your intro tone is not a style choice — it is a **brand signal**. It must match the voice you use for the entire video and every future video. A Hormozi-style opener on a soft, storytelling video creates dissonance and erodes trust. Choose the style that matches who you actually are on camera.
